data.name: Raid On Coasts
data.detailed_description:
Raid On Coasts is a real time strategy game set in a Massive Middle East themed land mass to cause chaos and carnage on !
The events of this work bear no resemblance to current events, this is a work of fiction.

Full story :

Recently, the expansion of the US has expanded through the construction of more military bases on the Russian borders .. But this is what increased the cup ... Russia decided to react and break the siege imposed by invading the Middle East from the gate of Yemen's coasts . .

The game offer you the ability to play with 2 armies :
  • Russian army
  • United States army
You can choose your role :
  • The attacker as the russian army , your mainly objective is to perform a raid on the coasts !
  • The defender as the united states army , your mainly objective is to defend the land from invaders

The map contain 14 different territories to capture :
  • Small villages
  • Big villages
  • Fuel factories

Features :



  • Massive Middle East themed land mass to cause chaos and carnage on

  • 2 Powerful armies to choose from

  • 8+ different units to play with

  • 14 territories to capture across the map

  • Gather resources upon capturing territories

  • Create a Command Base in order to call for support waves and rule the battle !

  • Every 30 seconds you can call for a new wave of units to land on the coasts

  • Order airstrikes on enemy units and positions !

  • Every week a new update containing new contents , ameliorations and bug fixes !

reviews.review:
[h1]Raid on Coasts[/h1]
...is a real-time strategy game. Tensions have reached the breaking point when war erupts between Russia and the United States of America over control of the Middle East.

[h1]⚙ [u]Game Description & Mechanics[/u] ⚙[/h1]
You start with a small squadron of soldiers in a map with about a dozen controllable outposts, each of which will supply you with funds, fuel and a spawn point for your troops and vehicles. The goal of the game is to control all the outposts, fortifying them and using their resources to have your troops advanced further. However, there is no set path between outposts, the enemy is free to circumvent your defenses and attack from any direction.

Once your soldiers have moved into an outpost, they must hold it a few seconds for the control to take over, after which they should move immediately to the next outpost, as your opponent will not wait to move theirs. When you've taken control of the outpost, you must renovate it, fortify it, and put it to work, selecting what trooper or vehicle to build within the confines of your budget. You must also defend it, or enemy troops will just walk in and take it from you.

[h1]☺ [u]What I enjoyed[/u] ☺[/h1]
You have a good variety of units to choose from, each with strengths and weaknesses, and you must carefully balance those. If your machine gun humvees face an armored tank, they're done for unless they have anti-tank backup. So while it's a race against the clock to control the outposts, it's also an anticipation game: you won't be able to build everything, so you have to figure out what your opponent will build to have the appropriate offensive or defensive equipment.

Having to capture fixed outposts, rather than building your own bases and buildings, makes it very different than typical real-time strategy games as it adds capture the flag elements to your tactics. After all, both factions are invading an established territory, so it makes sense to proceed in such a way.

[h1]☹ [u]What bothered me[/u] ☹[/h1]
There is a distinct missed opportunity in how the map is controlled. For the most part, the map is flat and open. Where are the mountains, the forests, the choke points? There is no way to have a proper control over the map as troops and vehicles can just drive in the open and go anywhere. Not that the opportunity to build fortifications and control passages would make much sense, as the single strategy to win this game is to rush: rush takeover the outposts, rush attack the enemy, every second that passes are seconds they are building more troops, so you can forget the idea of building a large army and taking your time meticulously conquering the map.

The game lacks any polish. Game menus are basic, rough-looking placeholders. There are little to no graphical options - not that the engine appears to make use of any special video technology, but...not even a resolution setting, really? The game's screenshots featured green and red lasers, and I was honestly hoping for a slightly more over-the-top G.I.Joe-esk setting, but those are not in the game that ends up offering a generic (if cliché) Russia-versus-USA setting in a semblance of real-world conflict.

[h1][b]My Early Access Verdict[/b]: ★☆☆ - [i]"Still a long way to go..."[/i][/h1]

When playing this, I found myself remembering playing [i][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/275530]Z[/url][/i] some 20 years ago, taking over outposts that had different strategic values, controlling the ways in and out of each outpost's zone by roads and bridges, and having fun in a wacky setting. But it is not the experience offered by [i]Raid on Coasts[/i]. Disregarding the bugs (such as the game not launching until I reboot my PC and try again), it is an unfinished game, missing the "fun" part. Yet, it is too soon to be considered abandoned. Some may argue that the last update is a year and a half ago, but that's exactly what they were saying with the update before that. The game is simply being developed slowly, so it may yet be redeemed. I will keep an open eye, and will gladly revise my review if it deserves it.

—————————————————————————
[i][b]This was just my opinion.[/b]

If you found this review helpful, please consider giving it a thumbs up, and feel free to check out more of my (purely opinionated) [url=http://steamcommunity.com/groups/CJsOpinions/]reviews[/url].[/i]
